basis: R8t frozen video.json in clean PR #1641 worktree

changes.before: Medium shot a writer gripping a tower rail while watching smoke rise from a city street, overcast light. Mid-seventeenth-century English setting: working-age figures in neckcloths and bodices; plaster or oak only where such materials fit the shot, with no East Asian robes
changes.after: Close shot inside a high stone lookout of the Tower on 2 September 1666, one English diarist in his thirties with a mature adult face, dark wool doublet and plain white neckcloth grips a thick stone parapet, a small plume of smoke above low tiled roofs visible through the narrow opening, soft overcast light. Tight frame on his face, stonework, roof tiles and smoke

changes.before: Medium shot a tower officer speaking to a diarist beside an unlettered city map, grey daylight. Year 1666: grown townsfolk wear felt hats, long coats or covered dresses; masonry or candle-era fittings if visible, not electric lights
changes.after: Medium shot inside a stone chamber of the Tower in 1666, one mature English tower official in a plain dark doublet and white falling band speaking aloud to a listener outside the frame with one open hand, a bare wooden table and arched stone window behind him, soft grey daylight

changes.before: Medium shot a thoughtful diarist looking out from a Tower window toward distant smoke, grey daylight. Restoration England: characters are adults in linen neckbands, fitted waistcoats and long gowns; old brickwork only where architecture appears, not present-day office gear
changes.after: Close shot inside the Tower on 2 September 1666, one English diarist in his thirties with a mature adult face, short dark hair, dark wool doublet and high white shirt collar leans forward to listen with a furrowed brow, a rough stone wall and narrow window behind him, soft grey daylight

changes.before: Medium shot a worried clerk in a riverboat viewing a burned house near city Bridge, cloudy daylight. English city life, 1666: fully grown residents in period hats, doublets or full skirts; plaster or oak details if walls or furnishings appear, avoiding modern signage
changes.after: Medium close shot from inside a small open wooden riverboat on the Thames on 2 September 1666, one English diarist in his thirties with a mature adult face, dark wool doublet and white neckcloth looks up at the scorched timber wall and sagging roof of a house beyond the boat rail. Tight frame on boat, man, damaged house wall and pale smoke under an overcast sky
